data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's subsumption argument proves too much and ignores correlated failure at the governance level. The claim that a large service can 'emulate' decentralization internally founders on Conway's Law-type coordination: central management can introduce systematic, correlated failure modes (e.g., a shared deployment pipeline, a common config error, a single security team's blind spot) that are structurally harder to avoid precisely because the subsystems are centrally managed. The problem explicitly asks about correlated failure; a centrally managed 'emulation' of diversity inherits the manager's correlated blind spots, so strictly more internal redundancy does not guarantee at-least-as-good resilience. The listed disanalogy/overturn condition gestures at this but the main claim's universal quantifier ('always at least as resilient') is directly refuted by common-cause failures introduced by central coordination itself.
